title: Competition and Consumer Amendment (Safeguarding the Reputation of Australian Beef) Bill 2017
short_title: Competition and Consumer Amendment (Safeguarding the Reputation of Australian Beef) Bill 2017

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would penalise cattle exporters for marketing beef as Australian when the cattle were slaughtered, or the beef was processed after slaughter, overseas.
It would also require exporters to take all reasonable steps to prevent products from that overseas slaughter or processing being marketed as Australian beef.
The proposed restriction would apply to people and companies engaged in cattle exporting, and would begin on the day after the bill received Royal Assent.
changes: A new pecuniary penalty provision would cover exporters who market the relevant products as Australian beef.
Exporters could also face a penalty for failing to take reasonable preventive steps.
The amendments would commence on the day following Royal Assent.
summary.affected: Australian cattle exporters, including companies, would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Rebekha Sharkie
speeches.brief: The speaker moved the second reading of the Competition and Consumer Amendment (Safeguarding the Reputation of Australian Beef) Bill, which would make it illegal to market beef as "Australian" unless it was processed under Australian standards and within Australia. The bill proposes maximum fines of $1.1 million for companies and $220,000 for individuals to protect the reputation of the Australian beef industry, which was worth $22.9 billion in the last year and supports 35,000 direct and 100,000 indirect jobs.
